Sam — really appreciate the RFP and the clear questions. High-level answers up front, then I’ll attach a short pricing spreadsheet and an annotated SOW.

1) Single-tenant compliance uplift: standard package includes isolated GPU pool (single-tenant tenancy), customer-managed KMS integration for key wrapping, and extended audit-log retention (90 days) with per-tenant log export. Optional add-ons: HSM-backed key stores (additional cost), custom audit-retention windows (beyond 90 days), and air-gapped control plane for on-prem review.

2) Reserved commits and guarantees: our commits are sold as reserved GPU capacity (e.g., 8x A100 equivalent nodes). We offer throughput SLAs tied to reserved size: a published tokens/sec baseline and a P95 latency SLO for topologies we certify. If you require a strict latency SLA, we can add a latency-backed credit schedule (subject to sizing validation).

3) Sizing heuristic: 30M tokens/month steady-state typically maps to a 2–3 node reserved pool if usage is spread over the month (no big spikes). If you need headroom for peak windows (bursting), we recommend a 4-node pool or burst policy. I’ll include rough cost/throughput lines in the spreadsheet.

Deliverables: RI_pricing_breakdown_OP-4821.xlsx (pricing tiers + uplift lines) and Draft_SOW_OptiHealth.docx (scope, SLAs, add-ons). Please confirm preferred KMS model (customer KMS via IAM role, or Redwood-managed KMS with HSM optional).

Ben — copied suggested approach below (keeping it tight and sale-friendly):

1) Pricing structure (4-node reserved commit, 24 months): base reserved rate = $62,000/month. Single-tenant compliance uplift = +12% of base (includes KMS integration + 90d audit + per-tenant exports). HSM and >90d retention are add-ons: HSM = +6% (one-time setup fee), extended-retention = +4% recurring.

2) Discounting: for a 24-month commit we can offer a one-time customer success credit equal to 8% of the first 6 months (applied as a service credit) — preserves list pricing while giving them up-front improvement. If procurement pushes on a recurring discount, cap recurring discount at 7% off base (not stackable with uplift reductions).

3) Latency SLA: offer conditional SLA: run a 2-week validation (after deployment) to certify the P95 targets. If we miss SLO in validated topology, offer a 15% credit of monthly reserved for affected windows (not retroactive). This avoids over-committing before sizing proof.

4) Trial of extended audit retention: offer 180-day retention trial for the first 3 months post-commencement; permanent extension is billable at +4% recurring.

5) Negotiation position: present uplift as a compliance package (not a tax) — show components and optionality in the workbook. Push HSM to be optional premium. Use the 8% upfront credit as the concession.

I annotated the pricing workbook with these lines. Happy to talk through redlines before you respond.

— Marissa
